1703.acip: [IV.241-8] ,ZAD PAR BYED TSUL NI, CHOS BZOD PA ZHI DANG 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA'I BAR CHAD MED LAM BRGYAD KYI SEMS PA GANG YIN PA RNAM PA BCU GNYIS PO DE NAG PO ZAD PAR BYED PA'I LAS YIN TE, 'DOD NYON SPONG BAR BYED PA'I PHYIR,
1703.wylie: [iv.241-8] ,zad par byed tshul ni, chos bzod pa zhi dang 'dod chags dang bral ba'i bar chad med lam brgyad kyi sems pa gang yin pa rnam pa bcu gnyis po de nag po zad par byed pa'i las yin te, 'dod nyon spong bar byed pa'i phyir
1703.english: Here is how these deeds are brought to an end. First let's take the twelve types of mental movement had with the four instants known as "the mastery of phenomena," as well as eight instants of the uninterrupted path [part of the path of seeing, the direct perception of selflessness] which is free of desire. These are the deeds that act to bring black deeds to an end, for they function to eliminate all the mental afflictions that relate to the desire realm.

1704.acip: BAR CHAD MED PA'I LAM DGU PA'I SEMS PA GANG YIN PA DE NI DKAR GNAG ZAD PAR BYED PA'I LAS YIN TE, 'DOD PA'I DGE BA LA 'DUN PA 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA'I SGO NAS SPONG , 'DOD PA'I NYON MONGS THOB PA CHAD PA'I TSUL GYIS SPONG BA'I PHYIR,
1704.wylie: bar chad med pa'i lam dgu pa'i sems pa gang yin pa de ni dkar gnag zad par byed pa'i las yin te, 'dod pa'i dge ba la 'dun pa 'dod chags dang bral ba'i sgo nas spong , 'dod pa'i nyon mongs thob pa chad pa'i tshul gyis spong ba'i phyir
1704.english: Next let's take that type which is the mental movement in the ninth instant of the uninterrupted path. This is a deed which acts to end the white and black, first of all because it eliminates desire-realm virtue by means of eliminating the aspiration, or the desire, for it. Secondly, it eliminates all the mental afflictions of the desire realm--the process here being that one stops the hold which retains them.

1705.acip: BSAM GTAN BZHI PA LA 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA'I BAR CHAD MED LAM SKYES PA THA MAS DKAR PO ZAD PAR BYED PA YIN TE, GZUGS KYI DGE BA LA 'DUN PA 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA'I TSUL GYIS SPONG BA'I PHYIR,
1705.wylie: bsam gtan bzhi pa la 'dod chags dang bral ba'i bar chad med lam skyes pa tha mas dkar po zad par byed pa yin te, gzugs kyi dge ba la 'dun pa 'dod chags dang bral ba'i tshul gyis spong ba'i phyir
1705.english: Finally, let's consider the final instant in the arising of the uninterrupted path which is free of desire for the fourth level of concentration. It is by this that white deeds are brought to an end, for here one eliminates aspiration, that is desire, for virtue of the formless realm. 65 Other Views on the Black and White

1763.acip: 'DOD PAR GTOGS PA'I YANG SKYES NAS THOB PA GCOD KYI, SBYOR BYUNG MI GCOD DE, LOG LTA CHUNG NGU'I CHUNG NGU'I GNAS SKABS SU DE'I THOB PA CHAD NAS MED PA'I PHYIR,
1763.wylie: 'dod par gtogs pa'i yang skyes nas thob pa gcod kyi, sbyor byung mi gcod de, log lta chung ngu'i chung ngu'i gnas skabs su de'i thob pa chad nas med pa'i phyir
1763.english: Even among the most basic virtues included in the realm of desire, only those which one had from birth can be lost--never those which have been acquired by applying some efforts in practice. This is because these latter types of virtue are gone by the time the mistaken views involved have even reached a minor stage of minor intensity. They have been lost because the hold retaining them was lost.

6915.acip: 'DOD PAR GTOGS PA'I YANG SKYES NAS THOB PA GCOD KYI, SBYOR BYUNG MI GCOD DE, LOG LTA CHUNG NGU'I CHUNG NGU'I GNAS SKABS SU DE'I THOB PA CHAD NAS MED PA'I PHYIR,
6915.wylie: 'dod par gtogs pa'i yang skyes nas thob pa gcod kyi, sbyor byung mi gcod de, log lta chung ngu'i chung ngu'i gnas skabs su de'i thob pa chad nas med pa'i phyir
6915.english: Even among the most basic virtues included in the realm of desire, only those which one had from birth can be lost--never those which have been acquired by applying some efforts in practice. This is because these latter types of virtue are gone by the time the mistaken views involved have even reached a minor stage of minor intensity. They have been lost because the hold retaining them was lost.

1702.acip: ,CHOS BZOD 'DOD CHAGS BRAL BA YI, ,BAR CHAD MED LAM BRGYAD KYI GANG , ,SEMS PA RNAM PA BCU GNYIS DE, ,NAG PO ZAD PAR BYED PA'I LAS, ,DGU PA'I SEMS PA GANG YIN PA, ,DE NI DKAR NAG ZAD BYED YIN, ,DKAR PO BSAM GTAN CHAGS BRAL BA'I, ,BAR CHAD MED LAM SKYES THA MAS,
1702.wylie: chos bzod 'dod chags bral ba yi, ,bar chad med lam brgyad kyi gang , ,sems pa rnam pa bcu gnyis de, ,nag po zad par byed pa'i las, ,dgu pa'i sems pa gang yin pa, ,de ni dkar nag zad byed yin, ,dkar po bsam gtan chags bral ba'i, ,bar chad med lam skyes tha mas
1702.english: Twelve types of mental movement had with Phenomena, mastery, and eight of the Uninterrupted path free of desire Are deeds that act to bring the black to an end. That which is the mental movement in the Ninth acts to end the white and black. White by the final uninterrupted arising, Free of desire for the concentration.

1432.acip: GZUGS MED DANG PO GSUM LA MI BRTEN TE, DE GSUM GYIS 'DOD PA LA MI DMIGS, MTHONG LAM GYIS 'DOD PA LA DMIGS PA'I PHYIR, SRID RTZE LA MI BRTEN TE, SRID RTZE NI 'DU SHES MI GSAL PA'I PHYIR,
1432.wylie: gzugs med dang po gsum la mi brten te, de gsum gyis 'dod pa la mi dmigs, mthong lam gyis 'dod pa la dmigs pa'i phyir, srid rtse la mi brten te, srid rtse ni 'du shes mi gsal pa'i phyir
1432.english: Neither can the ultimate stage rely upon any one of the first three formless levels, for at these levels one is incapable of focusing upon the desire level--and during the path of seeing one must. Finally, it is impossible for the ultimate stage to rely on the "peak" level--the fourth of the formless levels--for one's ability to discriminate at this level is too unclear.

1437.acip: ,GZUGS MED NA NI GZUGS KYI RJES 'BRANG MED PAS PHUNG PO BZHI PA CAN YIN NO,
1437.wylie: gzugs med na ni gzugs kyi rjes 'brang med pas phung po bzhi pa can yin no
1437.english: With regard to the formless realm, no accessory to knowledge possessing form would be present, and thus only four of the heaps had in attendance. 6 Nominal Accessories to Knowledge

1443.acip: THOS BYUNG NI 'OG MA GNYIS NA YOD KYI GZUGS MED NA MED DE, DE NA SGRA THOS PA MED PA'I PHYIR, BSAM BYUNG 'DOD PA NA YOD KYI GONG MA GNYIS NA MED DE, DE GNYIS NA SEMS PAR BRTZAMS PA TZAM GYIS TING NGE 'DZIN DU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, SGOM BYUNG NI GONG MA GNYIS NA YOD KYI 'DOD PA NA MED DE, 'DOD PA MNYAM PAR MA BZHAG PA'I SA PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
1443.wylie: thos byung ni 'og ma gnyis na yod kyi gzugs med na med de, de na sgra thos pa med pa'i phyir, bsam byung 'dod pa na yod kyi gong ma gnyis na med de, de gnyis na sems par brtsams pa tsam gyis ting nge 'dzin du 'gyur ba'i phyir, sgom byung ni gong ma gnyis na yod kyi 'dod pa na med de, 'dod pa mnyam par ma bzhag pa'i sa pa yin pa'i phyir
1443.english: Wisdom derived from learning is found in the lower two realms but never in the formless, since there is no hearing sound in that realm. Contemplative wisdom exists in the desire but not in the higher two realms, since there the mere act of starting to turn the mind towards an object sets off one-pointed concentration. Meditative wisdom, on the other hand, appears only in these higher realms and never in the desire, since it is not a level where there exists any controlled meditation.

1444.acip: BSTAN BCOS NI NGAG SGRA RANG BTZAN PA LA BYED NA 'DOD PA DANG BSAM GTAN DANG PO NA YOD KYI GNYIS PA YAN CHAD NA MED DE, RNAM RIG DPYOD DANG BCAS DAG NA, , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR, MING TSIG YI GE GSUM LA 'DOD PA LTAR NA KHAMS 'OG MA GNYIS NA YOD KYI GZUGS MED NA MED DE, 'DOD DANG GZUGS GTOGS SEMS CAN STON, , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
1444.wylie: bstan bcos ni ngag sgra rang btsan pa la byed na 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po na yod kyi gnyis pa yan chad na med de, rnam rig dpyod dang bcas dag na, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir, ming tshig yi ge gsum la 'dod pa ltar na khams 'og ma gnyis na yod kyi gzugs med na med de, 'dod dang gzugs gtogs sems can ston, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
1444.english: The classical commentaries, if we consider them as the actual sound of speech, exist only in the desire realm and are absent from the higher two: as the Treasure House itself reads, "Communicating at those with examining." If on the other hand we consider these commentaries as names, words, and letters, they can be said to exist in the lower two realms but not in the formless: again the Treasure House states, "Included in the desire, form; animate."

1533.acip: [IV.181-4] 'O NA, BSOD NAMS KYI LAS LA SOGS PA GANG ZHE NA, BSOD NAMS KYI LAS NI 'DOD KHAMS KYI DGE BA'I LAS DANG , MI G-YO BA'I LAS NI GONG MA GZUGS GZUGS MED LAS SKYES PA'I LAS YIN NO,
1533.wylie: [iv.181-4] 'o na, bsod nams kyi las la sogs pa gang zhe na, bsod nams kyi las ni 'dod khams kyi dge ba'i las dang , mi g-yo ba'i las ni gong ma gzugs gzugs med las skyes pa'i las yin no
1533.english: One might start with the following question: "Just how do you describe merit and the other types of deeds you mentioned?" Deeds that we call "merit" are the virtuous deeds of the realm of desire. What we call "unshifting" deeds are the ones that come from those realms above; that is, from the form and formless realms.

1535.acip: RNAM SMIN MI G-YO BA YIN TE, GANG GI PHYIR NA GZUGS GZUGS MED KYIS NI DE DAG TU SMIN PAR 'GYUR PA'I LAS KYI RNAM SMIN SA GZHAN DU NAM YANG MI SMIN PA'I PHYIR NA RNAM SMIN GZHAN DU MI G-YO BA'I PHYIR,
1535.wylie: rnam smin mi g-yo ba yin te, gang gi phyir na gzugs gzugs med kyis ni de dag tu smin par 'gyur pa'i las kyi rnam smin sa gzhan du nam yang mi smin pa'i phyir na rnam smin gzhan du mi g-yo ba'i phyir
1535.english: These deeds are called "unshifting" for the reason that a ripening of deeds which is meant to occur at "their" level--at the levels of the form and formless realms--will never occur at any other level. The point is thus that the ripening is an unshifting one.

1762.acip: ,JI LTA BU ZHE NA, 'DOD PAR GTOGS PA'I DGE RTZA GCOD KYI, GZUGS GZUGS MED KYI DGE RTZA MI GCOD DE, DE'I RGYUD LA DE MED PA'I PHYIR,
1762.wylie: ji lta bu zhe na, 'dod par gtogs pa'i dge rtsa gcod kyi, gzugs gzugs med kyi dge rtsa mi gcod de, de'i rgyud la de med pa'i phyir
1762.english: One may next ask how the process occurs. Most basic virtue which is taken in by the realm of desire can be lost, but not that which is taken in by the form or formless realms. This is because the types of views required can never appear in the mental streams of the beings of these realms.

24176.acip: BZOD PA BRGYAD NI, SDUG BSNGAL CHOS BZOD, RJES BZOD GNYIS, DE BZHIN DU, KUN 'BYUNG 'GOG PA LAM LA YANG SBYAR RO,,
24176.wylie: bzod pa brgyad ni, sdug bsngal chos bzod, rjes bzod gnyis, de bzhin du, kun 'byung 'gog pa lam la yang sbyar ro
24176.english: As for the eight states of mastery, we see the actual mastery of the truth of suffering; and the subsequent mastery of this same truth.  This continues in the same pattern for the truth of the source; the truth of the end; and the truth of the path.

36757.acip: GAL TE MTHONG LAM SDUG BSNGAL LA CHOS BZOD DES CHOS TE, RTEN 'BREL GYI GNAS LUGS STONG PA NYID MNGON SUM DU SHES PAS DE'I MJUG THOGS SU RTOGS BYA CHOS DBYINGS LA RNAM PA MI 'DRA BA MED DE,
36757.wylie: gal te mthong lam sdug bsngal la chos bzod des chos te, rten 'brel gyi gnas lugs stong pa nyid mngon sum du shes pas de'i mjug thogs su rtogs bya chos dbyings la rnam pa mi 'dra ba med de
36757.english: Suppose then that through the path of seeing-specifically, through the mastery of things relating to the truth of suffering-we perceive, directly, emptiness: the ultimate manner in which dependence exists. Subsequent to this point, the way of all things which is what we realize exhibits no differentiations.

24743.acip: [E137] YUL BDEN PA BZHIS BSDUS PA NYON MONGS PA DANG MI LDAN PA'I MTSAN NYID BZOD PA BZHI CHOS CAN, SPONG BA'I LAM YIN TE, BAR CHAD MED PA'I LAM GYI RNAM PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
24743.wylie: [e137] yul bden pa bzhis bsdus pa nyon mongs pa dang mi ldan pa'i mtshan nyid bzod pa bzhi chos can, spong ba'i lam yin te, bar chad med pa'i lam gyi rnam pa yin pa'i phyir
24743.english: Let us consider (58–61) the four states of mastery, which are subsumed by the object of the four higher truths, and characterized by not possessing anything involved with the negative emotions. These are paths of the elimination of undesirable qualities, Because they are aspects of the uninterrupted path. F. The ten perfections (aspects 62–71)
